text: {"claims":[{"claim_text":"A cache must not use heuristics to determine freshness when an explicit expiration time is present.","verdict":"SUPPORTED","reasoning":"Passage 1 directly states this prohibition.","citations":[{"index":1,"quote":"A cache MUST NOT use heuristics to determine freshness when an explicit expiration time is present in the stored response."}]},{"claim_text":"A response with Cache-Control: max-age=600 is never given a heuristic lifetime.","verdict":"SUPPORTED","reasoning":"Passage 0 identifies max-age as an explicit expiration mechanism, and passage 1 forbids heuristics when an explicit expiration time is present.","citations":[{"index":0,"quote":"using either the Expires header field (Section 5.3) or the max-age response directive (Section 5.2.2.1)"},{"index":1,"quote":"A cache MUST NOT use heuristics to determine freshness when an explicit expiration time is present in the stored response."}]},{"claim_text":"If a response with max-age=600 also has s-maxage=60, a shared cache treats it as fresh for 60 seconds.","verdict":"SUPPORTED","reasoning":"Passage 7 says s-maxage overrides max-age or Expires for a shared cache, so the shared cache uses the specified s-maxage value.","citations":[{"index":7,"quote":"The s-maxage response directive indicates that, for a shared cache, the maximum age specified by this directive overrides the maximum age specified by either the max-age directive or the Expires header field."}]},{"claim_text":"A shared cache must ignore any Expires header when s-maxage is present.","verdict":"SUPPORTED","reasoning":"Passage 8 explicitly says a shared cache recipient must ignore Expires when s-maxage is present.","citations":[{"index":8,"quote":"Likewise, if a response includes the s-maxage directive (Section 5.2.2.10), a shared cache recipient MUST ignore the Expires header field."}]},{"claim_text":"A client sending max-age=0 without max-stale is asking not to receive a stale response.","verdict":"SUPPORTED","reasoning":"Passage 3 says that unless max-stale is also present, the client does not wish to receive a stale response.","citations":[{"index":3,"quote":"Unless the max-stale request directive is also present, the client does not wish to receive a stale response."}]},{"claim_text":"proxy-revalidate applies only to shared caches.","verdict":"SUPPORTED","reasoning":"Passage 6 describes proxy-revalidate as applying to shared caches and says it does not apply to private caches.","citations":[{"index":6,"quote":"except that proxy-revalidate does not apply to private caches."}]},{"claim_text":"A private cache holding a stale response marked proxy-revalidate may reuse it without revalidating.","verdict":"CONTRADICTED","reasoning":"Passage 6 says proxy-revalidate does not apply to private caches, but passage 2 separately forbids a cache from generating a stale response unless it is disconnected or explicitly permitted; non-applicability of proxy-revalidate alone does not authorize stale reuse.","citations":[{"index":2,"quote":"A cache MUST NOT generate a stale response unless it is disconnected or doing so is explicitly permitted by the client or origin server (e.g., by the max-stale request directive in Section 5.2.1, extension directives such as those defined in [RFC5861], or configuration in accordance with an out-of-band contract)."}]},{"claim_text":"must-revalidate binds every cache.","verdict":"SUPPORTED","reasoning":"Passage 5 says in all circumstances a cache must not ignore must-revalidate.","citations":[{"index":5,"quote":"In all circumstances, a cache MUST NOT ignore the must-revalidate directive"}]},{"claim_text":"A disconnected cache must return an error instead of the stale response.","verdict":"SUPPORTED","reasoning":"Passage 5 explicitly requires an error response rather than reuse of the stale response when the cache is disconnected.","citations":[{"index":5,"quote":"if a cache is disconnected, the cache MUST generate an error response rather than reuse the stale response."}]},{"claim_text":"A client that sends max-stale=30 will accept a response up to 30 seconds past its freshness lifetime.","verdict":"SUPPORTED","reasoning":"Passage 4 says a max-stale value means the client accepts a response exceeding freshness lifetime by no more than the specified seconds.","citations":[{"index":4,"quote":"If a value is present, then the client is willing to accept a response that has exceeded its freshness lifetime by no more than the specified number of seconds."}]},{"claim_text":"A client that sends max-stale=30 will not accept a response that is 45 seconds stale.","verdict":"SUPPORTED","reasoning":"Passage 4 limits acceptance to no more than the specified number of seconds, so 45 seconds exceeds max-stale=30.","citations":[{"index":4,"quote":"If a value is present, then the client is willing to accept a response that has exceeded its freshness lifetime by no more than the specified number of seconds."}]},{"claim_text":"If two suitable responses are stored, a cache uses the one with the earlier Date header.","verdict":"CONTRADICTED","reasoning":"Passage 9 requires use of the most recent suitable response as determined by Date, not the earlier one.","citations":[{"index":9,"quote":"When more than one suitable response is stored, a cache MUST use the most recent one (as determined by the Date header field)."}]}]}
